title: 山居秋暝
author: 王维
intro: Rain has just passed over the mountains; moonlight falls through the pines and a spring runs over the stones. Wang Wei, the poet-painter, shows why people say his poems are paintings — and why he would rather stay here than go back to court.
analysis: 这首诗写山中雨后秋天的傍晚。“空山”不是没有东西，而是人少、安静、干净。中间两联最有名：明月从松树之间照下来，清泉在石头上流过——一句写光，一句写声，静中有动；竹林里传来笑声，原来是洗衣服的姑娘们回家了；荷叶摇动，原来是渔船顺流而下——先听见声音、看见动静，再说出原因，写得很有生活味。最后两句用了《楚辞》里“王孙兮归来”的典故：春天的花草谢了也没关系，秋天的山里一样美，我愿意留下来。宋代苏轼说王维“诗中有画”，这首诗就是最好的例子，也表达了诗人对官场之外清净生活的喜爱。
analysisEn: An autumn evening in the hills, just after rain. “Empty mountains” doesn’t mean nothing is there; it means quiet, few people, everything washed clean. The two middle couplets are the famous part. The bright moon shines down between the pines; a clear spring flows over the rocks — one line of light, one of sound, stillness with a little movement inside it. Then life appears: the bamboo rustles with laughter as the washerwomen head home; the lotus leaves sway as a fishing boat slips downstream. Notice the order — we hear the noise and see the movement first, and only then learn the cause, just as you would if you were standing there. The last couplet turns an old line from the Songs of Chu, which calls a wandering nobleman to come home from the wild hills. Wang Wei reverses it: let the spring flowers fade — autumn here is lovely enough, and the “nobleman” can happily stay. Su Shi later said Wang Wei’s poems contain paintings, and this poem is the classic example. It also shows his love of a calm life away from the court.
background: Wang Wei (701–761) was a high official, a painter, a musician and a devout Buddhist, often called the “Buddha of Poetry”. In mid-life he kept a country estate at Wangchuan in the Zhongnan Mountains south of Chang’an; this poem is usually linked to his retreats there.
pronunciation: 暝 míng（傍晚）。浣 huàn（洗衣）。喧 xuān。间 jiān（松间：松树之间）。歇 xiē。
version: 采用通行的教材版本，与《全唐诗》文本一致。

lines.lit: In the empty mountains, after fresh rain,
lines.en: The quiet hills, just washed by rain —

lines.lit: the weather, as evening comes, is autumn.
lines.en: with evening, the air turns to autumn.

lines.lit: The bright moon shines between the pines;
lines.en: Moonlight slants down between the pines,

lines.lit: the clear spring flows over the stones.
lines.en: a clear spring slides over the stones.

lines.lit: The bamboo is noisy: washing girls are returning;
lines.en: Laughter in the bamboo — the washing girls going home;

lines.lit: the lotus moves: a fishing boat goes downstream.
lines.en: the lotus leaves stir — a fishing boat drifting down.

lines.lit: Let spring’s fragrant flowers fade as they will;
lines.en: Let the flowers of spring wither if they must;

lines.lit: the young noble can still stay.
lines.en: a wanderer like me can stay on here.

words.note: “空”指安静、人少，不是什么都没有。

words.en: as one pleases; let it be
words.note: 现代汉语也常用，如“随意坐”。
古义；现代汉语“歇”多指休息，如“歇一会儿”。
原指贵族子弟，这里诗人指自己。

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 雨后的“空山”清新安静，是诗人心中理想的居所。
imagery.en: The rain-washed, quiet mountains are the poet’s ideal home.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 明月透过松林洒下清光，画面明净。
imagery.en: Moonlight filtering through the pines makes the whole scene clean and bright.

imagery.name: 松
imagery.zh: 松林与月光、清泉相配，写出山中的高洁与宁静。
imagery.en: Pines, moonlight and spring water together give the hills a pure, peaceful air.

imagery.name: 竹
imagery.zh: 竹林里的笑声带出浣女，山中不只有静，也有人间的温暖。
imagery.en: Laughter from the bamboo brings in the washing girls: the hills are not just quiet but warmly human.

imagery.name: 莲
imagery.zh: 莲叶摇动，引出顺流而下的渔船，静中有动。
imagery.en: Swaying lotus leaves reveal a fishing boat — movement inside the stillness.
